questionsToConsider: Which formats and lengths does your schedule actually have room for?
Do you review proposals anonymously? If so, keep the bio and headshot out of what reviewers see first.
Can you offer mentoring or travel support, and on what terms?
Will sessions be recorded, and do speakers get a real choice about it?
Do you want topic tracks as a question, so proposals sort themselves?
guide.howToUseResponses: Export the proposals to CSV and give reviewers only the title, abstract, takeaways, format and level, so they judge the talk before the name. Score each proposal on the takeaways, since vague ones usually mean a vague talk. Before building the schedule, pull out the workshop answers for room setup and capacity, and send the prerequisites to workshop attendees well ahead of the day.
customizeSteps: Change the format options to the slot lengths in your schedule, and keep the workshop questions only if you run workshops.
Rewrite the mentor and travel questions to say exactly what you offer, or remove them if you offer neither.
Add your deadline to the greeting, then share the link on your event site and social channels.

faqs.q: What should a call for speakers form include?
faqs.a: Contact details, a talk title, an abstract, concrete takeaways, the format and audience level, and a short bio. Anything else, like a headshot or a past talk, should be optional.

faqs.q: How long should a talk abstract be?
faqs.a: Long enough to explain what the talk covers and why it matters, short enough to fit in a printed programme. A couple of short paragraphs is usually right.

faqs.q: How do I encourage first-time speakers to apply?
faqs.a: Say plainly that first-timers are welcome and offer something concrete, like a mentor. This form only offers mentoring to people who have not spoken before, so experienced speakers skip it.

faqs.q: Can I ask workshop hosts different questions?
faqs.a: Yes. This template branches on the format, so only workshop proposals are asked about prerequisites, capacity and room setup.

doc.title: Call for speakers
doc.description: Take talk proposals in a shape a review committee can compare at a glance.

blocks.title: Got a talk in you? Tell us about it. Most people finish in about five minutes.
Which pronouns should we use in the programme?
Give us the abstract. What is the talk about, and why now?
blocks.description: This is what attendees will read in the programme, so write it for them.

blocks.title: Name three things someone will be able to do after your session.
blocks.description: One per line. Reviewers weigh this more than anything else, so make it concrete.

blocks.title: Which format fits the talk best?
What must attendees install or know before they arrive?
How many people can you teach at once?
What room setup do you need?
Write a short speaker bio, in the third person.
blocks.description: Two or three sentences, as it would appear on the website.

blocks.title: Add a headshot for the programme, if you have one.
Have you spoken at a conference before?
Share a link to a previous talk, video or slides.
Would you like a mentor to help you prepare?
blocks.description: We pair first-time speakers with someone who has done it before.

blocks.title: Would you need help with travel costs?
blocks.description: We ask everyone, and it never counts against a proposal.

blocks.title: Recording
blocks.consentText: If my talk is accepted, I agree that it may be recorded and the video and slides published after the event.

endings.title: Proposal submitted 🎤
endings.bodyMd: Thank you. We review proposals in batches after the deadline and reply to everyone, accepted or not.

closeRules.closedMessageMd: This form is no longer accepting responses.

requireAuth.message: Before we start, could you verify who you are? It only takes a moment.

steps.subject: You're {{remaining}} questions from finishing

steps.subject: Your {{form.title}} is still open
steps.bodyMd: Just a nudge in case it slipped. Your answers are still here whenever you're ready.
